name: Baruch the scribe
charge: Writing the roll from the prophet's mouth and reading it in the house of the Lord, and writing it again after the king burned it
summary: He wrote all the words of the Lord from Jeremiah's mouth on a roll, and because the prophet was shut up, he read it in the house of the Lord on a fast day in the ears of all the people. The princes heard it and told him to hide with Jeremiah. Jehoiakim cut the roll with a penknife and burned it leaf by leaf. Baruch wrote it again from Jeremiah's mouth, and many like words were added. He sought great things for himself and was told not to, and given his life for a prey.
offense: Baruch wrote the words Jeremiah dictated and read the roll in the Lord's house when Jeremiah could not go there. He then read it before the princes. The work required more than copying: he publicly delivered a warning that placed both him and the prophet in danger. After Jehoiakim burned the roll, Baruch wrote again at Jeremiah's mouth, preserving all the former words and many like words added. The king's attack did not cause him to abandon the charge. Yet Baruch also knew weariness and grief, crying that the Lord had added sorrow to his pain and that he found no rest.
judgment: The Lord answered Baruch's distress by setting it within the judgment coming upon the land. What God had built He would break down, and what He had planted He would pluck up. Baruch was not to seek great things for himself amid that overthrow. God promised him his life for a prey in all places where he went. Preservation, rather than worldly advancement, was the particular mercy pledged to him. The faithful scribe was not promised freedom from the nation's troubles, but life through them.

verses.text: Then Jeremiah called Baruch the son of Neriah: and Baruch wrote from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the Lord, which he had spoken unto him, upon a roll of a book.
And Jeremiah commanded Baruch, saying, I am shut up; I cannot go into the house of the Lord:

Therefore go thou, and read in the roll, which thou hast written from my mouth, the words of the Lord in the ears of the people in the Lord’s house upon the fasting day: and also thou shalt read them in the ears of all Judah that come out of their cities.
It may be they will present their supplication before the Lord, and will return every one from his evil way: for great is the anger and the fury that the Lord hath pronounced against this people.
And Baruch the son of Neriah did according to all that Jeremiah the prophet commanded him, reading in the book the words of the Lord in the Lord’s house.

entries.commentary: In the fourth year of Jehoiakim, the Most High tells Jeremiah to take a roll of a book and write in it all the words He has spoken against Israel, against Judah, and against all the nations, from the days of Josiah until that day. The purpose is that the house of Judah, hearing all the evil purposed against them, might return every man from his evil way so that He would forgive their iniquity and their sin.

Jeremiah calls Baruch the son of Neriah, who writes from Jeremiah's mouth all the words of the Most High upon the roll. Because Jeremiah is shut up and cannot go into the house of the Most High, he sends Baruch to read the roll in the ears of the people on the fasting day, that they might present their supplication and turn from their evil way, for great is the anger and fury pronounced against this people. Baruch does all that the prophet commanded, reading the book of the words of the Most High in the Most High's house.

In the fifth year of Jehoiakim, in the ninth month, a fast is proclaimed before the Most High to all the people in Jerusalem and those who came from the cities of Judah. Baruch reads the words of Jeremiah in the temple in the chamber of Gemariah, in the ears of all the people. Michaiah the son of Gemariah, having heard the words, goes down into the king's house to the scribe's chamber where all the princes are sitting, and declares to them all he had heard when Baruch read.

The princes send Jehudi to bring Baruch with the roll, and they ask him to sit and read it in their ears. When they hear all the words they are afraid, both one and another, and say they will surely tell the king; they ask Baruch how he wrote all these words, and he answers that Jeremiah pronounced them with his mouth while Baruch wrote them with ink in the book. The princes tell Baruch to go hide himself and Jeremiah, and to let no man know where they are.

The princes lay up the roll in the chamber of Elishama the scribe and tell all the words in the ears of the king, who sends Jehudi to fetch it and read it before him and the princes. The king sits in the winter house in the ninth month with a fire burning on the hearth; as Jehudi reads three or four leaves, the king cuts them with a penknife and casts them into the fire until the whole roll is consumed. Neither the king nor his servants are afraid nor rend their garments; though Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah make intercession that he not burn the roll, he will not hear, and he commands that Baruch and Jeremiah be seized, but the Most High hides them.

After the king burns the roll, the word of the Most High comes to Jeremiah to take another roll and write all the former words that Jehoiakim had burned. Against Jehoiakim He pronounces that he shall have none to sit upon the throne of David, his dead body shall be cast out to the heat by day and the frost by night, and He will punish him, his seed, and his servants for their iniquity. Jeremiah gives a second roll to Baruch, who writes from Jeremiah's mouth all the words of the burned book, and many like words are added besides.
